editorLatency.qualification: Local measurements, with concurrent test activity in both stages. Observed latency is higher; these samples do not isolate the implementation from machine load and do not establish a speed improvement.

analyzerChanges: Assignments and unpacking use one binding-contract check.
Tuple arity and recursive per-position facts participate in bindings, returns, indexing and widening.
Homogeneous literal diagnostics reuse the recursive field comparison.
runtimeSimplifications: Array and tuple returns reuse ArrayBindingContract.
Removed whole-array observed-cell union settlement; first concrete lazy cell establishes a contract, subsequent demanded cells are checked.
Recursive element merging uses the shared contract merger.

verification.cli: Initial full run: 482/486 passed, with two SQL fixture subtest failures, their parent failure, and generated reference mismatch. After fixes all 33 affected CLI checks passed, including a new tuple SQL round-trip test. All terminal tests passed in the full run. The complete npm test command was not rerun after fixes.
verification.demos: 392 files, zero failed; after final named-row selection changes all 10 Kaggle files passed again.
verification.finalReview: 65 tuple and collection tests passed after final review; TypeScript build and both repository boundary checks passed.

migrations: Mixed positional returns and test bundles use tuple.
Ordinary numeric arrays use explicit consistent integer or real cells.
JSON flat value column is text; numeric consumers convert explicitly.
Mixed JSON arrays and parse captures produce tuples; homogeneous results remain arrays.
eigh, weighted graph edge pairs and SQL parameter bundles use tuples.
SQL NULL fixtures use absent object fields rather than the distinct JSON null label.
limitations: Runtime validation is still required for unresolved static facts.
Lazy specialization and boundary declarations remain steps 3 and 4.
No packed-storage optimization or runtime speed improvement is claimed.
